introduction--docs.content: import { Meta } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks"; # Carbon Components Ember An Ember implementation of IBM's [Carbon Design System](https://carbondesignsystem.com), kept in parity with [`@carbon/react`](https://react.carbondesignsystem.com). ## Installation ```sh pnpm add carbon-components-ember @carbon/styles pnpm add -D sass ``` ### Compatibility - **Ember:** tested against `ember-source` 7 (the current release), and in CI against the beta and alpha channels too. - **Apps:** it's a v2 addon. Embroider/Vite apps work as-is; classic ember-cli apps need `ember-auto-import` 2. Apps compile its stylesheets, so they need `sass`. Load Carbon's styles and the addon's own stylesheet once, in your app's entry point: ```ts import "@carbon/styles/css/styles.css"; import "carbon-components-ember/styles.scss"; ``` Some components render elsewhere in the page, so add their two targets to your application template: ```gts ``` ## Usage Import components straight into your `.gts` templates: ```gts import { Button } from "carbon-components-ember/components"; ``` Services are namespaced under `carbon.`: ```ts import { service } from "@ember/service"; class MyComponent { @service("carbon.notifications") notifications; } ``` Every component page in the sidebar is generated from the component's own Glint signature: the args table, blocks and element come straight from the source, and each story doubles as a browser test. Stories follow Carbon React's: the same pages, names and variants, and each story file lists any React story it can't match yet. ## Use with AI agents The package ships an [agent skill](https://agentskills.io) for coding agents: how to use the components, how Carbon's React-based docs and designs carry over to Ember, and these docs for the version your app has installed. With pnpm 12.11 or later, approve it once with `pnpm approve carbon-components-ember`. The [README](https://github.com/IBM/carbon-components-ember#use-with-ai-agents) covers the requirements, and the steps for TanStack Intent, npm and Yarn. [`carbon-components-ember-mcp`](https://github.com/IBM/carbon-components-ember/tree/main/carbon-components-ember-mcp#readme) serves the same docs over MCP, and gives agents the skill's instructions when they connect. Add it from your app's directory, for example in Claude Code: ```sh claude mcp add carbon-components-ember -- npx -y carbon-components-ember-mcp ```
